To go or come into an enclosed or partially enclosed space.

examples.text: You should knock before you enter, unless you want to see me naked.

We determined that the car driver’s transportation of multiple teen passengers, limited driving experience, and likely impairment from effects of cannabis at the time of the crash adversely affected her judgment of the danger of entering the intersection in front of the approaching combination vehicle.

glosses: To cause to go (into), or to be received (into); to put in; to insert; to cause to be admitted.

examples.text: to enter a knife into a piece of wood
to enter a boy at college, a horse for a race, etc.

glosses: To go or come into (a state or profession).

examples.text: My twelve-year-old son will be entering his teens next year.
She had planned to enter the legal profession.
Until 2008 there was denial over what finance had become. … But the scandals kept coming, and so we entered stage three – what therapists call "bargaining".

glosses: To type (something) into a computer; to input.

examples.text: Enter your user name and password.

glosses: To record (something) in an account, ledger, etc.

examples.text: Each amount entered in the debit column of the journal is posted by entering it on the credit side/column of an account in the ledger.

glosses: To become a party to an agreement, treaty, etc.

examples.text: I am pleased to notify the Congress of my intent to enter into a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) with the Government of Singapore.

glosses: To become effective; to come into effect.

examples.text: This Act shall enter into force on 01 March 1998.

glosses: To go into or upon, as lands, and take actual possession of them.
To place in regular form before the court, usually in writing; to put upon record in proper from and order

examples.text: to enter a writ, appearance, rule, or judgment

glosses: To make report of (a vessel or its cargo) at the custom house; to submit a statement of (imported goods), with the original invoices, to the proper customs officer for estimating the duties. See entry.
To file, or register with the land office, the required particulars concerning (a quantity of public land) in order to entitle a person to a right of preemption.

examples.text: Under existing laws governing the qualifications of an alien to enter 160 acres or more of the public domain he is only required to file his declaration of intent to become a citizen.

glosses: To deposit for copyright the title or description of (a book, picture, map, etc.).

examples.text: entered according to act of Congress

glosses: To initiate; to introduce favourably.

examples.text: This sword but shown to Caesar, with this tidings, / Shall enter me with him.

glosses: To begin (a regular activity or job); to undertake; to take up.

examples.text: […] I entered, that same day, on a regular occupation of pushing Miss Havisham in this chair […] round her own room, and across the landing, and round the other room.

glosses: Alternative spelling of Enter (“the computer key”).
Alternative spelling of Enter (“a stroke of the computer key”).
To put in between or into.

examples.text: In order to withdraw money from a cash machine, you have to insert your debit card.
To make your proof easier to understand, I recommend you insert a few more steps.

glosses: An image inserted into text.
A promotional or instructive leaflet inserted into a magazine, newspaper, tape or disk package, etc.

examples.text: This software can print compact disc inserts if you have the right size of paper.

glosses: A mechanical component inserted into another.

examples.text: a threaded insert

glosses: An expression, such as \"please\" or an interjection, that may occur at various points in an utterance.
A sequence of DNA inserted into another DNA molecule.
A pre-recorded segment included as part of a live broadcast.
A close-up shot used to draw attention to a particular element of a larger scene.

examples.text: […] close-ups of her legs on the escalator, an insert of the emergency stop button (ARRET D'URGENCE), intercut close-ups of her glance and the cinema sign, […]

glosses: A diaper insert.
A plug-in that adds an effect to an audio track.
A key to toggle between text insert mode and overwrite mode
To put (something) in its usual storage place; to place out of the way, clean up.

examples.text: Please put away the tools when you are finished.
I put the clothes away so as to neaten the room.

They burned the old gun that used to stand in the dark corner up in the garret, close to the stuffed fox that always grinned so fiercely. Perhaps the reason why he seemed in such a ghastly rage was that he did not come by his death fairly. Otherwise his pelt would not have been so perfect. And why else was he put away up there out of sight?—and so magnificent a brush as he had too.

glosses: To store, add to one's stores for later use.

examples.text: putting a little away for a rainy day
Preparing for the worst, they put away food for the winter.

glosses: To consume (food or drink), especially in large quantities.

examples.text: You wouldn't think such a small person could put away so much food.
The blonde one, old Bernice, was drinking bourbon and water. She was really putting it away, too.

glosses: To send (someone) to prison or mental asylum.

examples.text: After he was convicted, they put him away for 10 years.

glosses: To kill someone.

examples.text:
It's Decoration Day.
And I knew the Hill Boys would put us away,
but my Daddy wasn't afraid.
He said "We'll fight till the last Lawson's last living day"

glosses: To knock out an opponent.

examples.text: He put away his opponent in the first round.

glosses: To discard, divest oneself of.

examples.text: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things.

glosses: To fend off, deflect; to dismiss.

examples.text: Also he told kynge Arthur that he shold mysse hym / yet had ye leuer than al your landes to haue me ageyne / A sayd the kynge / syn ye knowe of your aduenture puruey for hit / and put awey by your craftes that mysauenture / Nay said Merlyn it wylle not be / soo he departed from the kynge.

glosses: To divorce.

examples.text: And the pharyses cam and axed hym a question: whether it were laufull for a man to putt awaye hys wyfe.

glosses: To take a large lead in a game, especially enough to guarantee victory or make the game no longer competitive.

examples.text: They put the game away by scoring three touchdowns in the fourth quarter.

glosses: To strike out a batter.
To catch a fly ball or tag out a baserunner.
(pickleball) To hit the ball in such a way that the opponent cannot reach it; see passing shot
To place inside.

examples.text: Just put in the key for the ignition and turn it.

glosses: To place inside.
To imprison or place in a prison cell.

examples.text: They put me in the state pen for a year for that.
They put me in with an absolute maniac for a cellmate.

glosses: To apply, request, or submit.

examples.text: I'm going to the bank to put in for a transfer.

glosses: To contribute.

examples.text: I put in an extra hour at work today.
Despite his success, the comedian liked to put in appearances at some of the smaller venues.

glosses: To call at (a place or port), especially as a deviation from an intended journey.

examples.text: We put in at Brixham, a most excellent fishing Town, but very dirty and disagreeable.
“They were bound for Quebec—hadn’t any notion of coming to P. E. I. They had a long rough voyage and water got scarce, so the captain of the New Moon put in here to get some.

glosses: To declare or make official

examples.text: The defendant has put in a plea of not guilty.

glosses: To plant a crop.

examples.text: We've put in carrots in the east field.

glosses: To make (a telephone call).
To fill in on a form or questionnaire; to use as an answer on a form or questionnaire.

examples.text: Put in my name as your emergency contact.

glosses: To install or deliver.

examples.text: I'm putting in a new water heater in the spring.

glosses: To injure the body of (someone).

examples.text: She put six shots in him.

glosses: To distribute type that is ready for composing.
A place, stead.
To put something away in a compact and tidy manner, in its proper place, or in a suitable place.
To store or pack something in a space-saving manner and over a long time.

examples.text: Yet everybody knows that a cargo properly stowed in a seaworthy craft reaches market in much the better condition than by rail, though perhaps it is some hours longer on the way.

glosses: To arrange, pack, or fill something tightly or closely.
To dispose of, lodge, or hide somebody somewhere.

examples.text: Ar.[…]The Marriners all vnder hatches ſtowed, / Who, with a Charme ioynd to their ſuffred labour / I haue left aſleep :[…]

glosses: To cease; to stop doing something.

examples.text: But when I strove my flame to tell, / Says she, 'Come, stow that patter, / If you're a cove wot likes a gal, / Vy don't you stand some gatter?' / In course I instantly complied— / Two brimming quarts of porter, / With sev'ral goes of gin beside, / Drain'd Bet the Coaley's daughter.
“Come, come,” said Silver; “stow this talk. He’s dead, and he don’t walk, that I know; leastways, he won’t walk by day, and you may lay to that. Care killed a cat. Fetch ahead for the doubloons.”

glosses: A cry used by falconers to call their birds back down to hand.

examples.text:
His seconde hawke wexyd gery […]
on the rode loft
She perkyd her to rest.
The fauconer then was prest,
Came runnynge with a dow,
And cryed, ‘Stow, stow, stow!’
But she wold not bow.

glosses: Introducir, insertar o meter algo dentro de otra cosa.
Hacer injertos (inserción de yemas de una planta en otra).
Incluir o insertar en un texto notas, imágenes, etc.

examples.text: Como en la anterior etapa he injerido un fragmento de Cervantes furtivamente en mi prosa, voy a injerir en esta segunda jornada otro párrafo de la pobre Angela

glosses: Intervenir o participar, con cierta influencia o interferencia, en un asunto, situación o proceso.

examples.text: asistimos a un cínico y calculado propósito de encontrar argumentos para injerir en este jugoso mercado internacional de las remesas
